summary:

Theja De Silva, Group Chief Financial Officer, Nawaloka Hospitals PLC Colombo, and CA Sri Lanka Best CFO of the Year 2026.

Theja De Silva, Group Chief Financial Officer of Nawaloka Hospitals PLC, Colombo, has been named Best CFO of the Year 2026 at the 47th National Conference of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (CA Sri Lanka), recognising his contribution to financial leadership and business transformation.

For De Silva, the recognition marks an important milestone in a career shaped by navigating challenging business environments and a belief that financial leadership goes far beyond managing numbers.

His professional journey includes working with organisations facing financial and operational difficulties, experiences that helped shape his approach to business recovery, governance and sustainable growth. Today, at Nawaloka Hospitals PLC Colombo, he has played a key role in strengthening financial discipline and contributing to the Group's financial turnaround, while supporting continued investment in healthcare services and innovation.

Reflecting on his leadership philosophy, De Silva said, "The true strength of a CFO lies not merely in understanding numbers, but in translating financial knowledge into sound decisions, inspiring people and creating opportunities for progress. Finance should not simply explain business performance after the event; it should help shape an organisation's future."

Holding professional qualifications including ACCA, FCPM and MSLID, De Silva also serves as Secretary of AAT Sri Lanka, extending his contribution beyond corporate leadership to the development of the accounting and finance profession. He is particularly passionate about encouraging young professionals to look beyond traditional accounting roles and embrace opportunities in strategic business leadership.

He attributes his professional growth to four essential pillars: knowledge, experience, soft skills and networking, believing that a combination of these qualities is fundamental to effective leadership.

De Silva expressed his gratitude to Nawaloka Hospitals PLC Colombo Chairman Dr. H. K. Jayantha Dharmadasa, Deputy Chairperson Anisha Dharmadasa, the Board of Directors and his colleagues for their continued trust and support.

He hopes the recognition will inspire emerging finance professionals to pursue excellence with integrity, sound judgement and a commitment to making a meaningful difference.

title: IPS calls for targeted wealth taxation, says VAT cuts premature | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:00
-     - 104

Sri Lanka should shift part of its tax burden towards accumulated wealth and assets through targeted measures rather than a comprehensive net wealth tax, the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) said, cautioning that VAT cuts would be premature and further rate hikes are highly unlikely.

In its flagship report, Sri Lanka State of the Economy 2026, released in early October, the think tank said revenue gains since 2022 have been driven primarily by high tax rates. Rising living costs, pressures on businesses and concerns regarding competitiveness are fuelling calls for tax relief, particularly reductions in VAT.

“Tax increases are often effective during crisis periods, but may generate diminishing economic and political returns if maintained indefinitely,” the report said. 

High consumption taxes can disproportionately affect lower-income households, particularly when real wages remain under pressure. Although inflation has moderated substantially from its 2022 peak, poverty levels remain elevated and household consumption has yet to fully recover, the IPS said, concluding that further increases to statutory tax rates are highly unlikely.

Yet relief would be premature. “Reducing VAT before achieving a broader and more efficient tax system could reverse recent fiscal gains and place additional pressure on debt sustainability,” the IPS said. Tax compliance remains uneven, informality remains widespread and numerous exemptions continue to reduce potential revenue collection, it noted. Sri Lanka’s tax-to-GDP ratio, though substantially improved since 2022, remains below that of many emerging Asian economies and still falls short of the level required to sustainably finance public services, social protection and debt obligations.

The way out, the report argued, lies in broadening the tax base and improving the balance between direct and indirect taxation, with wealth at the centre. “Wealth taxation can improve social welfare by shifting part of the tax burden away from productive activities and consumption towards accumulated wealth and assets. This is one of the least distortionary forms of taxation, generating a stable source of revenue,” it said.

High-income households command a disproportionate share of national income and wealth, the IPS noted. They are also associated with more resource-intensive consumption patterns, resulting in a larger share of total emissions than the lower-income group.

However, the think tank ruled out a levy on total net assets. “Wealth taxation should not be a comprehensive net wealth tax, but rather a targeted strengthening of existing tax instruments linked to wealth and high incomes,” it said.

That would mean modernising property taxation through updated valuation, digital cadastres (computerised registers of land ownership and boundaries) and improved enforcement. 

It would also mean streamlining the taxation of capital gains and rental incomes, given the significant share of wealth accumulated through asset price appreciation, particularly in land and real estate markets. Complementary taxation of luxury and high-value assets could enhance progressivity, the report said.

The IPS also singled out high-income professionals. Tax non-compliance is often concentrated in income streams outside formal withholding systems, where tax is not deducted at source, including professionals in medicine, law, consultancy, construction and private education, it said. 

“Expanding electronic invoicing, strengthening taxpayer identification systems, integrating banking and tax information, and using data analytics to identify high-risk taxpayers could significantly improve compliance and broaden the tax base,” it added.

title: Sri Lanka needs IMF beyond 2027 to counter ‘debt overhang’ | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:00
-     - 91

With Sri Lanka’s current IMF Extended Fund Facility (EFF) program set to end in March 2027, the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) has made a case for continued engagement with the Fund, warning that the country faces a prolonged ‘debt overhang’ of elevated borrowing costs and limited market access as it exits debt distress.

In its flagship report, Sri Lanka State of the Economy 2026, released in early October, the think tank said a precautionary relationship with multilateral institutions could help the country through the post-restructuring transition. 

“In this context, maintaining a precautionary relationship with multilateral institutions, including the possibility of a successor IMF-supported arrangement, may provide an important credibility anchor during the post-restructuring transition,” it said. 

Such engagement could help sustain policy discipline and reduce sovereign risk premia, the extra return investors demand to lend to a government, while structural reforms aimed at export diversification, reserve accumulation and fiscal consolidation take root.

The IPS said Sri Lanka’s return to international capital markets remains structurally constrained by elevated sovereign risk premia and sub-investment-grade credit ratings. The result has been persistently high external borrowing costs relative to historical norms.

“Empirical evidence from frontier-market sovereigns suggests that countries exiting debt distress episodes typically face a prolonged period of ‘debt overhang’ in international markets, during which spreads remain elevated and market access is either limited or prohibitively expensive,” the IPS said. Spreads are the additional yield investors demand over benchmark Bonds to compensate for a borrower’s risk.

The report cautioned against an early dash for market funding. 

“Against this backdrop, premature or large-scale reliance on commercial external borrowing would likely increase rollover risks and reintroduce external liquidity pressures before reserve buffers and export earnings are sufficiently strengthened,” it said. Rollover risk is the danger that a government cannot refinance maturing debt on affordable terms.

The challenge is compounded by heightened global uncertainty and repeated exposure to external shocks, the think tank said. These include climate variability associated with El Niño-Southern Oscillation cycles and extreme weather-related disruptions, which could amplify macroeconomic volatility and weaken investor risk appetite.

Sovereign fragility is determined not solely by debt levels but by the interaction between external debt composition, reserve adequacy and shock exposure, the report said. Where economies remain highly exposed to terms-of-trade and climate-related shocks, market-based financing tends to be pro-cyclical: it flows in during good times and dries up when most needed, reinforcing rather than smoothing external vulnerabilities. 

Durable market re-entry typically requires not only fiscal adjustment but also sustained improvements in external resilience and institutional credibility, it added.

The IPS also called for greater debt transparency. It warned that any deterioration in fiscal space tends to increase incentives for governments to hide the true extent of their debt, by moving it off-budget or by using financial or natural assets as collateral for additional borrowing. Before the crisis, Sri Lanka maintained off-budgetary mega development projects in ports, aviation, water supply and sanitation, and power and energy.

Average total capital spending on these projects amounted to approximately 1.3% of GDP during 2017-2020, with foreign financing contributing around 0.7% of GDP. The existing Integrated Treasury Management Information System (ITMIS) does not cover the full project lifecycle, the IPS said, making a unified digital public financial management system covering revenue, expenditure and debt data across all institutions ‘imperative’.

Noting that Sri Lanka’s debt default and economic crisis were partly due to governance failure, the report proposed a fiscal council, operationally independent from the Ministry of Finance. The council would provide independent macro-fiscal forecasts, cost key revenue and expenditure measures, monitor fiscal risks such as contingent liabilities and state-owned enterprise obligations, and report regularly to Parliament and the public.

title: World Bank Group launches first digital strategy to expand access and create jobs | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:00
-     - 42

The World Bank Group yesterday launched its first digital strategy, bringing together its public and private sector capabilities to help developing countries expand affordable digital access, improve services, and create jobs.

The strategy addresses four priorities: expanding connectivity; making devices and data more affordable; strengthening digital services and skills; and helping countries build the foundations to benefit from artificial intelligence.

“Digital technology can help countries create jobs and make scarce resources go further. Realizing that potential requires a comprehensive approach—from reliable connectivity and affordable devices to digital skills and useful services,” said World Bank Group President Ajay Banga. “Our first digital strategy brings these pieces together, helping countries build the foundations to benefit from today’s digital tools and the promise of small AI—AI for the people.”

The launch comes as developing countries face twin challenges: constrained resources and a growing need for jobs. Over the next 10 to 15 years, 1.2 billion young people will reach working age in developing countries, while their economies are projected to create about 420 million jobs.

Digital technology can support job creation across the World Bank Group’s five priority sectors: infrastructure and energy, agribusiness, health care, tourism, and value-added manufacturing. It can help businesses reach customers, improve productivity, and access finance, while reducing the cost of delivering public services.

Yet substantial barriers remain. Over 2 billion people were offline globally in 2025. Only 23 percent of people in low-income countries used the internet, compared with 94 percent in high-income countries. Many people live within network coverage but cannot afford a smartphone or data, lack digital skills, or have limited access to services relevant to their needs.

The strategy sets out four areas of action:

Safeguards—from privacy to cybersecurity and fraud protection—run across all four priorities.

The strategy brings together the World Bank Group’s financing, policy advice, private investment, and guarantees around country priorities. It also provides a basis for working with governments, technology companies, development partners, and philanthropy to extend digital opportunities to more people and businesses. Its aim is to help countries turn digital access into higher productivity, better services, and more opportunities to earn a living.

Complementing the strategy’s AI readiness and adaptation priority, the World Bank Group also announced the AI Infrastructure and Readiness Initiative. This is a new effort to help governments in emerging markets access affordable compute capacity—and put small AI to productive use—through shared, pay-as-you-go GPU infrastructure (specialized computing power used to develop and run AI applications), offering a practical alternative to standalone national data centers. The initiative will have an initial focus on Africa and Latin America, with knowledge partners including Cassava Technologies and NVIDIA.

title: Connect to Care brings global expertise together to accelerate citizen-focused digital transformation | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:00
-     - 65

Connect to Care (CTC), a Sri Lankan non-governmental organisation working alongside government, philanthropic and development partners, has established a seven-member Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) Advisory Panel and launched “Give Back”, a structured program enabling Sri Lankan professionals worldwide to contribute expertise to priority digital transformation initiatives.

Together, the initiatives are designed to connect international experience, specialist knowledge and local implementation capabilities with government-led priorities, with a clear focus on translating digital transformation into measurable improvements in citizens’ lives.

The Advisory Panel comprises Illango Patchamuthu, Indika De Zoysa, Karthik Subramanian, Vajira Weerasekera, Chandi H. Dharmaratne, Vishaka Nanayakkara and Keith De Alwis. 

Collectively, they bring experience spanning global development, digital policy, enterprise technology, artificial intelligence, Digital Public Infrastructure, digital health, organisational transformation, academia and large-scale technology implementation.

Illango Patchamuthu brings more than three decades of international development experience, including senior World Bank leadership and, most recently, his role as Director, Strategy and Operations in its Digital and AI Vice Presidency. Indika De Zoysa contributes approximately three decades of experience across technology, digital policy, industry development and public-private collaboration, including senior leadership at Huawei Technologies Lanka.

Karthik Subramanian, former Global Chief Technology Officer of Global Fashion Group and former CTO of ZALORA, brings extensive experience in scaling digital platforms, data capabilities and consumer-facing technology businesses. Vajira Weerasekera adds more than three decades of technology leadership across Asia, Europe and the United States, including senior roles at Red Hat and Microsoft, with expertise spanning cloud, AI and enterprise transformation.

Chandi H. Dharmaratne contributes more than 25 years of leadership experience across the United States and Asia-Pacific, with expertise in organisational transformation, workforce strategy and AI-enabled HR modernisation. Vishaka Nanayakkara, Senior Lecturer in Computer Science and Engineering at the University of Moratuwa, brings expertise across e-governance, ICT for Development, digital education and national capacity building. Keith De Alwis brings more than two decades of experience at the intersection of technology, program delivery and digital health. His career includes serving as Group Chief Digital Officer at Hemas Holdings and co-founding Telenor Health, where he held CTO and COO responsibilities. 

The Panel will provide independent strategic and technical guidance as CTC supports government-led priorities across DPI, digital agriculture, healthcare and broader public-service transformation. Its role will include reviewing approaches, identifying capability gaps, connecting relevant expertise and helping institutions prepare for sustainable adoption.

CTC will continue to work within existing national programs and institutional mandates rather than establish parallel systems. Its focus is on strengthening coordination, addressing specific capability gaps and supporting implementation where additional technical or strategic capacity can accelerate agreed priorities.

Connect to Care Chairman Chandita Samaranayake said: “Digital transformation succeeds when policy, technology, institutions, financing and people move together. Our role is to strengthen the work already underway, connect the right expertise to specific needs and support partners in moving from strategy to implementation. The Advisory Panel gives us access to independent global experience while complementing the practical capabilities of our program teams and consultants.”

Central to CTC’s approach is the principle that digital transformation should ultimately be measured by what changes for citizens. Depending on the program, this could include easier access to healthcare, more timely information for farmers, reduced travel and waiting times, lower transaction costs or improved access to government services.

CTC intends to incorporate measurable citizen outcomes, program milestones and user feedback into the way relevant initiatives are assessed, helping institutions understand not only whether systems have been delivered, but whether they are creating practical value.

Alongside the Advisory Panel, Give Back creates a structured pathway for Sri Lankan professionals working internationally across DPI, AI, digital transformation and related disciplines to contribute their expertise to validated programs in Sri Lanka.

The program will match expertise and availability with defined capability gaps. Contributions may range from technical advice and program reviews to mentoring, knowledge transfer and targeted implementation support. Engagements will be linked to clearly defined deliverables and intended outcomes.

“Give Back is about turning goodwill into practical contribution,” Samaranayake added. “Sri Lanka has exceptional professionals working across technology and transformation globally. By connecting that expertise with validated needs and accountable programs, we can create a credible channel through which knowledge and experience contribute directly to national priorities.”

The Advisory Panel will operate on a voluntary, pro-bono basis, with members participating in their individual capacities. Over time, CTC aims to build the initiative into a broader platform for two-way knowledge exchange between Sri Lanka and other markets across the Global South, strengthening local capability while sharing lessons from Sri Lanka’s own transformation journey.

Vidullanka PLC, in partnership with David Pieris Motor Company today inaugurated the 10 MW DPV Solar Power Plant in Ranna, making significant strides in Sri Lanka’s renewable energy journey. Developed under the joint venture company DPV Solar Energy Ltd., the plant was declared open by Energy Deputy Minister Eng. Arkam Ilyas and the Sri Lanka Sustainable Energy Authority Director General Eng. Rohana Randombage.

Vidullanka also submitted winning bids to implement 18.7MW/93MWh of battery energy storage systems (BESS) at its operational solar plants under the NSO’s 150 MW BESS tender. The successful collaboration between Vidullanka and David Pieris signals the power of partnerships in creating meaningful impact in the renewable energy space. This extends into the consortium’s development of Lot 2 of the 50 MW Mullikulam wind power plant, where they emerged as the lowest cost bidder in the tender. title: From spice trade to spice science: BOI pitches in Rome | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 06:18
-     - 247

BOI Chairman Duminda Hullangamuwa

The Board of Investment of Sri Lanka (BOI) has presented Sri Lanka’s flagship agri-food investment opportunities at the Hand-in-Hand Initiative Investment Forum 2026, convened by the Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations (FAO) in Rome from 13 to 16 October. 

Chairman Duminda Hulangamuwa led the BOI delegation, accompanied by Director General Dr. Sulakshana Jayawardena.

Sri Lanka’s presentation, “Unlocking Premium Export Markets through Value Addition and Product Differentiation”, framed a new pitch: the future of traditional trade lies in the global botanical market, where science reveals what makes Sri Lankan spices unique and turns that knowledge into products that heal, nourish and care. The world already values the Ceylon name; the next stage of growth lies in capturing more of that value at home.

Premium quality, limited returns

The Chairman recalled that Sri Lanka has stood at the centre of the global spice trade for centuries, and its smallholder farmers still produce some of the world’s most recognised agri-food products. Yet much of that value is captured overseas, because Sri Lanka exports raw commodities rather than value-added products. The binding constraints, he said, are access to capital, technology and premium markets, which are exactly what international investors can bring.

From red ocean to blue ocean

Exporting spices in bulk is a classic “red ocean”: a crowded market where many origins compete on volume and price, and margins are steadily squeezed. That is not where Sri Lanka’s future lies.

Instead, the BOI is turning to a “blue ocean” of high-value, botanical extract-based markets built on properties unique to Sri Lankan produce. Ceylon Cinnamon is true cinnamon (Cinnamomum verum), naturally very low in coumarin compared with the cassia that dominates world trade. Ceylon black pepper is prized for its pungency and piperine content, and centuries of Ayurvedic knowledge add a provenance that global brands increasingly seek.

Global Market Insights values the botanical extracts market at about $ 30 billion in 2024, rising to $ 64.6 billion by 2034. The Global Wellness Institute puts the wider wellness economy at $ 6.8 trillion, forecast to reach $ 9.8 trillion by 2029.

Four high-value export opportunities

The BOI presented four investment-ready value chains worth $ 65.1 million, expected to reach some 21,100 direct and more than 84,000 indirect beneficiaries.

 Cinnamon offers the highest projected return, building a premium nutraceutical industry around a spice Sri Lanka already exports at around $ 250 million a year. Sea cucumber offers the largest income gain, an estimated $ 4,800 per person, while coffee would revive a crop for which Ceylon was once among the world’s leading exporters.

Spice science: Technology meets tradition

The future of traditional trade lies in the laboratory as much as on the plantation. DNA barcoding can authenticate true Ceylon Cinnamon and distinguish it from cassia, protecting its origin and its premium. Chemical profiling can identify the active constituents that give each spice its character, such as cinnamaldehyde and eugenol in cinnamon and piperine in black pepper. Building on centuries of Ayurvedic use, research into these compounds can create evidence-based applications in health, wellness and beauty care: in effect, healing people with spices.

The BOI’s pitch is aimed squarely at technology-driven companies: extraction and biotechnology firms, nutraceutical and pharmaceutical formulators, and beauty and wellness brands. Genomic authentication, supercritical CO₂ extraction, standardisation of bioactive compounds, clinical validation and precision formulation can unlock the medicinal, wellness and beauty value already present in Sri Lankan produce:

n Ceylon Cinnamon: standardised low-coumarin extracts, oils and natural actives for nutraceuticals, functional foods, oral care and cosmetics, moving from a price per kilo to a price per gram.

n Ceylon black pepper: high-purity oleoresins and piperine for supplement and pharmaceutical formulators.

n Sea cucumber: marine collagen, peptides and bioactive compounds for premium beauty and skincare.

n Ceylon coffee: speciality-grade coffee alongside green coffee extracts and coffee-cherry ingredients.

n Ayurveda and provenance: traceability, geographical indications and certification that turn Sri Lankan origin into brand equity.

In this model, investors bring technology, research and access to global brands, and Sri Lanka brings unique raw materials, heritage and communities ready to supply them. More of the value is created and kept in Sri Lanka.

Why invest in Sri Lanka

Investors gain up to 100% foreign ownership, backed by 26 investment protection agreements; free trade agreements with India, Pakistan and Singapore, and preferential access to the European Union and the United Kingdom; the Port of Colombo at the heart of East–West shipping routes; a reduced 15% corporate income tax rate for services exports; and an educated, English-speaking workforce.

Next steps for investors

The BOI invited investors to explore the investment note on Sri Lanka’s Hand-in-Hand country page and request bilateral meetings. It will follow up with investors met in Rome and actively target technology-driven companies to establish value-added operations in Sri Lanka, positioning the country as a source of unique, high-value natural actives rather than a bulk commodity supplier.

title: SLID launches Women In Leadership intake 4 | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 06:09
-     - 119

SLID Women Directors Forum Chair Sandra De Zoysa, SLID Chairman Dinesh Weerakkody

The Sri Lanka Institute of Directors (SLID) is set to launch the fourth intake of its flagship Women in Leadership program on 21 October 2026, reaffirming its commitment to strengthening the pipeline of women ready to take on leadership and board-level responsibilities in Sri Lanka’s corporate sector.

To be held at the City Club Meeting Room, Cinnamon Grand, the six-month program is designed to support second-tier female executives, women directors and aspiring female leaders as they prepare to navigate the increasingly complex demands of senior leadership and the boardroom.

The program comes at a time when organisations are placing greater emphasis on diversity, strong governance and developing a sustainable leadership pipeline. Through a combination of structured learning, mentoring and networking, SLID’s Women in Leadership program seeks to equip participants not only with the knowledge required for boardroom leadership, but also with the confidence and strategic perspective needed to progress their careers.

The program incorporates mentoring sessions with experienced Board Directors, a one-day intensive leadership program tailored specifically for women leaders and dedicated career support. Participants will also have opportunities to network with leading corporate figures in Sri Lanka and gain access to the SLID Women Directors Forum, together with its membership benefits and resources.

Those who successfully complete the program will receive a certificate of completion and gain entry to SLID’s prestigious directory of Women Directors and Board Ready Women, providing an additional platform for visibility and future board opportunities.

SLID Women Directors Forum Chair Sandra De Zoysa said:  “The Women Directors Forum is committed to accelerating the advancement of women onto Boards across all sectors and to building a strong, lasting female leadership pipeline. Participants in this program will gain a real understanding of boardroom dynamics and the responsibilities that make a director effective, learn from experienced Board Directors and experts in governance, regulation and technology, and share experiences with one another to solve the challenges women face in the boardroom. They will also build networks across industries and disciplines, position themselves strategically for the next stage of their careers, strengthen their personal brand, and achieve a healthier work-life balance. Our aim is to prepare women to take their seat at the table with confidence and credibility.” 

SLID Chairman Dinesh Weerakkody emphasised that developing women for leadership is increasingly a strategic business imperative for Sri Lankan organisations.

“The high levels of migration in recent years, coupled with the large pool of educated women in Sri Lanka, make it not only the right thing to do, but also smart business practice. Ensuring the full participation of women in corporate decision-making is now an imperative,” he said.

Reflecting on the response to previous program, Weerakkody noted that participants had consistently described the initiative as a source of significant learning, personal development and inspiration. He said the strong feedback and continuing need to build a stronger pipeline of women leaders made the continuation of the program particularly timely.

With only 25 places available for the upcoming intake, SLID is encouraging corporates to identify and nominate emerging women leaders and invest strategically in building a more diverse and inclusive leadership pipeline for the future.

title: Colombo forum advances South Asia’s circular economy agenda | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 06:09

The Regional Forum on Circular Economy in South Asia enters its second and final day today (20), at the Taj Samudra, Colombo, with discussions scheduled on a regional framework and implementation roadmap for a resource-efficient, competitive and inclusive economy.

The Federation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Sri Lanka (FCCISL) President and SAARC Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SAARC-CCI) Senior Vice President Dr. Rohitha Silva delivered the opening remarks on 19 October.

Jointly convened by SAARC-CCI and FCCISL, the Regional Forum on Circular Economy in South Asia is organised in collaboration with the Institute for Global Environmental Strategies, through its Centre Collaborating with UNEP on Environmental Technologies (IGES-CCET), and HELP-O Sri Lanka.

Environment Minister Dr. Dammika Patabendi is scheduled to deliver today’s keynote address on enabling policies and supportive mechanisms for circular economy development. The first-day program listed keynote addresses by ESCAP’s Subregional Office for South and South-West Asia Director Mikiko Tanaka, participating online and Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe.

Other dignitaries listed in the two-day program include Foreign Affairs Deputy Minister Arun Hemachandra, Embassy of Nepal Chargé d’Affaires a.i. Vijay Kumar Raut, and SAARC-CCI and FCCSIL former President Deshabandu Mackay Hashim.

Technical contributors included IGES-CCET Director Dr. Premakumara Jagath Dickella Gamaralalage, IGES and the Japan Partnership for Circular Economy Dr. Yasuhiko Hotta, Thammasat University Dr. René van Berkel, and IGES Research Director Dr. Ngoc-Bao Pham.

Under the theme “From International Practice to a Regional Framework and Action Roadmap”, the forum connects international experience with business opportunities and implementation priorities.

The circular economy retains the value of products and materials through better design, efficient resource use, maintenance, repair, reuse and recycling. These practices can reduce waste, improve productivity and create enterprise opportunities.

Six priority sectors are covered: textiles and ready-made garments; plastics and packaging; agriculture; electrical and electronic waste; construction and demolition; and tourism.

FCCISL State Affairs Committee Director and Chairman Ruwan De Silva emphasises the importance of linking circular economy initiatives with enterprise development, district economies, investment and inclusive growth.

The first-day program focused on experiences from Japan, ASEAN and other relevant contexts, alongside opportunities for youth, start-ups and women-led enterprises, with working sessions addressing financing, technology, standards and market barriers.

Today’s program will review the draft Framework for a Resilient and Inclusive Circular Economy in South Asia and refine its proposed 2026–2030 roadmap, including responsibilities, financing needs and milestones.

Participants will also consider a proposed SAARC-CCI Colombo Declaration on Circular Economy in South Asia, with further endorsement processes to follow.

Recognition of informal workers and waste collectors forms part of the proposed approach. The forum aims to translate regional cooperation into practical partnerships, investable projects and lasting benefits for businesses and communities.

The visits provided an opportunity to explore trade and investment opportunities in Sri Lanka, strengthen business-to-business (B2B) linkages, and promote greater economic engagement between India and Sri Lanka.

The CII delegation, comprising representatives from diverse sectors including healthcare and pharmaceuticals, solar energy, information technology, manufacturing, and footwear, held a series of meetings with key stakeholders in Sri Lanka. The CCCI delegation, representing sectors such as healthcare, logistics, building materials, business consultancy, information technology, and tourism, also held a series of engagements with Sri Lankan stakeholders. The delegation met Deputy Minister Abeysinghe and senior officials of the BOI. The delegation also held B2B meetings with various Sri Lankan companies to explore potential business partnerships and opportunities for collaboration. As part of its visit, the delegation toured the manufacturing facilities of Nestlé and Elephant House to gain first-hand exposure to industrial operations in Sri Lanka.

Both delegations also called on Indian High Commissioner Santosh Jha. During the interactions, the High Commissioner shared his perspectives on the Sri Lankan economy and the growing opportunities for Indian businesses in Sri Lanka. He encouraged the visiting companies to deepen their engagement with Sri Lankan counterparts, establish business partnerships, and explore opportunities for trade and investment.

The visit of the CCCI delegation also forms part of the High Commission’s ongoing efforts to strengthen economic and commercial engagement with Sri Lanka at the regional and sub-national levels, by facilitating greater interaction between regional business chambers and enterprises from different parts of India and their Sri Lankan counterparts. The visits of the two delegations underscore the continued efforts to strengthen India-Sri Lanka economic and commercial ties through enhanced B2B engagements and institutional partnerships.

Sri Lankan para athlete Janani Dhananjana made an impressive mark at the 2026 Asian Para Games by winning the silver medal in the women’s T47 200 metres final, clocking a personal best of 25.80 seconds.

Dhananjana delivered a memorable performance on the continental stage, demonstrating remarkable determination, speed and competitive ability against some of Asia’s leading para sprinters. Although she has competed internationally before, this was her first appearance in the women’s T47 200 metres event at international level, making her medal-winning performance particularly significant.

Thailand’s Sasirawan Inthachot claimed the gold medal, finishing in 25.23 seconds, just 0.57 seconds ahead of Dhananjana in a closely contested final.

The silver medal represents an important milestone in Dhananjana’s sporting career, especially as she achieved a personal best in her first international appearance in the 200m T47 event. Her performance also provided Sri Lanka with another encouraging result at the prestigious continental competition.

Targets more medals

Dhananjana will compete in two more of her preferred events at the Asian Para Games 2026: the women’s T47 100 metres and the women’s T47 long jump. She will be looking to build on her impressive 200m performance and add further medals to Sri Lanka’s tally.

Her speed and acceleration will be valuable assets in the 100 metres, where a powerful start and the ability to maintain maximum speed are crucial. Having already demonstrated her sprinting ability in the 200m, she will aim to carry that momentum into the shorter-distance event.

In the long jump, her sprinting speed can provide an advantage during the run-up, while explosive take-off power, balance and landing technique will play important roles in achieving a competitive distance.

With a silver medal and a personal best already secured, Dhananjana has every reason to approach her remaining events with confidence. While both competitions will present tough challenges, her performance in the 200m offers plenty of encouragement for what lies ahead.

Her achievement highlights the growing potential of Sri Lankan para athletics and the dedication of athletes representing the country on the international stage. Sri Lankan sports fans will now eagerly await her performances in the women’s T47 100m and long jump, hoping she can continue her impressive campaign and bring home further medals

summary:

Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne yesterday informed Parliament that he had received copies of 30 petitions filed against the Sri Lanka Cricket Bill, and 30 against the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill. The Supreme Court’s determination on the Bills’ constitutionality will be announced in the House before they are debated.

The Cricket Bill, presented to Parliament on 6 October, 2026 by Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Sunil Kumara Gamage, would make Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) a statutory body run by a 14-member Board of seven Independent and seven Elected Directors. It would also introduce a three-tier voting system, under which District Cricket Associations would operate through Provincial Cricket Associations.

Some of the petitions argue that the 25 district associations would lose voting rights, and contests the President’s appointment as SLC Patron and the Minister’s power to replace an administration with a three-member committee. SLC has been run by a Cricket Transformation Committee headed by Eran Wickramaratne since the previous administration resigned in April. The Bill provides for elections within six months of its passage.

title: Star-class all-round performance by Minhas knocks England over | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 00:07
-     - 9

RAWALPINDI: A star-class all-round performance by 21-year-old Arafat Minhas who scored a fifty and took six wickets with his left-arm spin saw Pakistan defeat England by 87 runs at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium yesterday and secure back to back wins in the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series.

On Sunday, Pakistan began the Tri-Series with a win against Sri Lanka and now have one foot in the final.

England began their chase of 303 brightly but it ended in complete disaster as they were bowled out for 215 in 39 overs. Ben Duckett (45 off 46 balls, 8 fours) and Tom Banton (57 off 53 balls, 5 fours, 2 sixes) added 91 off 87 balls at better than run-a-ball. England were cruising until Duckett top-edged a pull off Haris Rauf. After that it became a slide as Arafat Minhas came onto bowl.

Having already made a 50 with the bat, he took that confidence to the ball and simply outclassed England. Banton pulled a short ball to mid-wicket, Harry Brook was left surprised by the turn which opened him up completely, Jordon Cox was trapped in front. Jamie Overton and Will Jacks holed out while Adil Rashid was also trapped in front to give Minhas his second five-fer in 5 ODIs – 6/40 off 8.4 overs. He became only the third Pakistani to perform the double of a fifty and five wickets in an ODI after Abdul Razzaq and Shahid Afridi.

In between, Naseem Shah and Haris Rauf gave their team the advantage by dismissing Joe Root and Sam Curran. It was a total team effort and a sensational comeback from Pakistan who have taken a big step towards reaching the 31 October final.

Earlier, Pakistan did well to breach the 300-run mark after they had stumbled earlier in the innings. Fakhar Zaman departed off the very first ball of the game. Saim Ayub was bounced out cheaply by Sonny Baker soon after. Babar Azam got off to a good start but he was struggling against the spin of Will Jacks and he was knocked over by the off-spinner courtesy one that turned in sharply. The centurion from the last game, Salman Agha, played one shot too many and holed out in the process to Rashid.

Pakistan were in a spot of bother at 81-4 but their lower middle-order and lower order bailed them out of trouble. Hasan Nawaz batted positively from the word go and kept finding the boundaries regularly while young Saad Baig showed good composure and grit. Baig though fell attempting a pull shot for 35 after helping Nawaz add 52 off 53 balls. Nawaz found another able ally in Arafat Minhas. Minhas was dropped twice (not easy chances) by Cox and he made his opportunities count. He batted sensibly and played the ball on its merit. Nawaz (79 off 74 balls, 5 fours, 4 sixes) and Arafat (59 off 58 balls, 9 fours) both struck fifties to help the cause of their side adding 78 off 74 balls. Faheem Ashraf’s 26-ball 39-run cameo (5 fours, 1 six) and his 72-run stand off 49 balls with Minhas in the death overs allowed Pakistan to maintain their momentum and finish with a good score. The English bowlers were particularly good in the middle overs but lost a bit of rhythm towards the fag end. It was a tough day for them, not least the returning Adil Rashid and Sam Curran. But Baker emerged with three wickets, while Jacks and Overton were excellent through the middle overs. 

Scores: 

Pakistan 302-9 (50) (Babar Azam 34, Saad Baig 35, Hasan Nawaz 79, Arafat Minhas 59, Faheem Ashraf 39, Gus Atkinson 2/35, Sonny Baker 3/65) beat England 215 (38.4) (Tom Banton 57, Ben Duckett 45, Joe Root 33, Haris Rauf 2/32, Arafat Minhas 6/40)
